methodological_rigor.justification: Robust prediction modeling study using appropriate advanced statistical methods. LASSO regression with cross-validation optimization is properly employed for variable selection, followed by multivariable Cox regression. Model validation includes ROC curves, calibration plots, decision curve analysis, and 500 bootstrap resamples for internal validation. Authors explicitly address time-dependent HSCT confounding and justify 3-year endpoint. Sample size is modest (136 patients, 22 deaths, 28 relapses) leading to acknowledged wide confidence intervals, but analytical approach is rigorous for the study type.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Retrospective prognostic model development study directly applicable to pediatric AML risk stratification and treatment planning. While not an intervention trial, nomograms with strong discrimination (AUC 0.79-0.91) and calibration directly inform clinical decision-making regarding consolidation intensity and HSCT timing. As a prognostic model based on case series, maps to LoE 4 per Oxford CEBM, but clinical utility is high. Findings enable individualized risk assessment rather than population-level recommendations.

reporting_quality.justification: Manuscript follows prediction model reporting standards with clear population definition, variable selection rationale, model development details, and validation methodology. Strengths include transparent discussion of missing data handling (random forest imputation), inclusion of supplementary tables and figures, and explicit statistical code description (R version). Gaps include: no explicit data availability statement or mention of model code sharing, no pre-registration, and limited detail on access to AML-CAMS trial data for external validation feasibility.

novelty_literature.justification: The study develops first nomograms for pediatric RUNX1::RUNX1T1-positive AML predicting 3-year outcomes using Chinese cohort data. While High-Risk MRD, WBC group, and treatment regimen as prognostic factors are not novel individually, their integration into a validated prediction model represents meaningful methodological advancement. The finding that MRD, treatment regimen, and WBC independently predict OS (not previously quantified in nomogram form) extends prior work. However, core prognostic concepts are established; the contribution is primarily in model development rather than discovery.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-structured manuscript with clear introduction establishing clinical context and knowledge gaps. Methods are comprehensive and transparent, results systematically presented with figures and supplementary materials. Discussion thoughtfully contextualizes findings within existing literature, addresses mechanistic explanations for prognostic factors, and explicitly acknowledges limitations including single-center bias, modest cohort size, and limited genomic data. Writing is precise and accessible. Minor areas for improvement include some length in methods section, but overall publication-ready quality is evident.

key_strengths: Rigorous prognostic model development with strong internal validation (bootstrap AUC 0.79-0.91 across outcomes)
Clinically actionable nomograms integrating MRD dynamics, baseline disease burden, and treatment regimen for individualized risk stratification
Appropriate LASSO and multivariable Cox regression methodology with decision curve analysis demonstrating net clinical benefit
Transparent acknowledgment of limitations including single-center bias, modest event count, and HSCT confounding by indication
key_concerns: Single-center Chinese cohort with modest sample size (n=136, 22 deaths, 28 relapses); wide confidence intervals for High-Risk MRD indicate statistical instability
Retrospective design with regimens assigned by trial period rather than concurrent randomization; temporal changes in supportive care confound outcome comparisons
Limited genomic profiling (KIT and RAS only); other mutations and co-mutation patterns not uniformly available, reducing mutation-based prognostic signal detection
External validation in prospective multicenter setting not yet performed; generalizability to non-Chinese populations unclear
No explicit data sharing plan or model code availability stated
chief_reviewer.rationale: Well-conducted single-center prognostic model study developing internally validated nomograms for pediatric t(8;21) AML with strong discrimination and calibration. Appropriate methodology and clinically meaningful outcomes support tier-2 journal placement pending multicenter external validation. Retrospective design and single-center origin require acknowledgment but do not negate clinical utility for risk stratification in patient populations.
